items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: My teacher there was Alexander Valentine, who had been to Europe with Jim Europe. Everybody remembers Jim Europe.

ctx.x: So in later years in Atlantic City when I was going to school, I remember one day standing outside of a tavern and hearing "Black and Tan Fantasy" (I didn't know who it was at the time, but naturally later I found it was Duke Ellington) and the "East Toodle-Oo," and I think that's what really turned me on to be a musician.

So Bordentown School up in Bordentown, New Jersey, which was about 19 miles from Trenton, had a band that used to travel all over the state, they came to our school, and after hearing this band I just had to go. Fortunately, my parents were able to send me to this school. And that was my beginning as a musician. My teacher there was Alexander Valentine, who had been to Europe with Jim Europe. Everybody remembers Jim Europe.
